extracted_factors.Label: Rising Life Expectancy
extracted_factors.Description: Hong Kong has one of the highest life expectancies, which increases the years individuals spend in retirement.

extracted_factors.Label: Gender Differences in Retirement Preparation
extracted_factors.Description: Survey indicates that women plan less for retirement than men, affecting their financial security in later years.

extracted_factors.Label: Medical Inflation
extracted_factors.Description: Medical costs are rising at a rate faster than general inflation, affecting the financial preparedness of the elderly.

extracted_factors.Label: Social Isolation
extracted_factors.Description: Social isolation has increased due to COVID-19, affecting both mental health and social engagement among the elderly.

extracted_factors.Label: Retirement Age Increase
extracted_factors.Description: The retirement age in Hong Kong has been increased to 65, affecting workforce dynamics and opportunities for younger workers.

extracted_pain_points.description: Many Hong Kong residents feel there is insufficient financial support from the government for productive ageing.
Rising medical costs and lack of sufficient insurance coverage are major concerns for the elderly.
Social isolation and loneliness among the elderly have been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.
Women are more financially vulnerable in retirement due to reliance on spouses and traditional social roles.
